name: Arcwelder
label: Touch and Go
lede: Two Graber brothers and a drummer who sings got sued out of their first name by the company that makes the Tilt-A-Whirl, made four albums for Touch and Go around their day jobs, and came back twenty-four years later with a record mixed by J. Robbins.

eras.title: Named after a carnival ride, then sued by it
eras.text: Minneapolis in the late 1980s had Hüsker Dü and The Replacements as proof a local band could matter. Tilt-A-Whirl played the 7th St Entry about twice a month, put out a debut on a friend's label, and lost the name just as the record came out.

years.src: Discogs: Arcwelder · The Current: Minneapolis post-punks Arcwelder
years.h: Scott Macdonald and Rob Graber start Tilt-A-Whirl; Rob brings his brother
years.p: Macdonald, a drummer and singer out of Minneapolis bands Red Letter Day and Velvet Elvis, teams up with Rob Graber. [[Bill Graber|93e344cb-0498-4424-928e-443f835dc7e9]] joins, and the brothers swap bass and guitar between songs.
years.xp: Everyone writes and everyone sings: Macdonald and Bill Graber trade lead vocals, and Discogs notes the Grabers switching instruments. Rob later explained his bass tuning to The Current: all four strings in D. "It sounds great live," he said.

years.h: 'Pint of Blood' is the first single, on Sonic Boom
years.p: A 7-inch with 'Define My Life' on the flip.

q: It's probably the place that we feel most comfortable playing.
years.h: The 7th St Entry becomes a second home
years.p: From 1989 to 1992 the band plays the Entry about twice a month, at least 29 shows there in all, and opens for [[Soul Asylum|b10db9ad-b4c3-47f3-a7a4-37864b134f65]] and [[Babes in Toyland|41593aa1-dda6-4a5a-af87-0eebf93e3775]].

The debut comes out on the label run by Chris Johnson of [[Rifle Sport|54f70716-5cef-43e0-99c1-d91b5bd518b4]], with a release show at the 7th St Entry on January 27. About half the live set made the record.
years.xp: [[Grant Hart|571e1aad-0512-45ec-a26d-1d09d786cc53]] of Hüsker Dü told the band they reminded him more of [[Mission of Burma|db9d25d7-a85b-4a29-b2ff-8f5b69ed691e]] than of his own band, the New Puritan ReView reported. Bill Graber named Gang of Four and Rifle Sport as influences.

years.h: The Tilt-A-Whirl's manufacturer sues, and the band changes its name
years.p: Sellner Manufacturing, maker of the ride, sues for trademark infringement as This is coming out. Rather than go to court the band renames itself after an instrumental on the record.
years.xp:
Bill Graber told the New Puritan ReView they'd considered and dropped The Tilted World and Tilted Whirled. They'd skipped 'Arcwelder' as a band name before because it sounded too industrial.

First copies of This carried a sticker saying the band had nothing to do with the ride's maker.

eras.title: John Peel, New Order and a Touch and Go deal
eras.text: Two records with producer Brian Paulson got the band heard in Britain, where John Peel and New Order picked up on it. Then Touch and Go signed them, and Pull became the record people still bring up.

years.src: Star Tribune: Arcwelder wields its first new music in 24 years · Discogs: Arcwelder
years.h: Jacket Made in Canada, the first record with Brian Paulson
years.p: Still on Big Money Inc. Bill Graber later said the Paulson sessions were "very collaborative."

years.h: 'Favor' lands at No. 32 in John Peel's Festive Fifty
years.p: The BBC DJ's listeners vote it in. That year New Order, guest-editing NME, also make the band their punk rock single of the week.

years.h: A Beatles cover, a Prince cover and a first Touch and Go single
years.p: Big Money puts out 'I Am the Walrus' backed with 'Sign o' the Times', and [[Touch and Go|83a554c5-4fd3-4ec8-9dd5-15989850ea17]] releases 'Raleigh' as TG105.

years.src: Magnet: Lost Classics, Arcwelder 'Pull' · Star Tribune: Arcwelder wields its first new music in 24 years
years.h: Pull, the first Touch and Go album
years.p: Made again with Paulson. Magnet later called it "a 45-minute masterpiece" that holds its own against anything from indie rock's best years.
years.xp: Magnet's 2009 Lost Classics piece pegged them as Hüsker Dü's logical successor: a punk-rooted pop trio with guitarist and drummer sharing vocals. It also said they never got past cult status.

years.h: Opening the Smashing Pumpkins' Siamese Dream release party
years.p: Arcwelder plays the Chicago party for the [[Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]]' 1993 album.

eras.title: Touring with the Jesus Lizard, home for work
eras.text: The band kept its day jobs and a steady pace: three more Touch and Go albums in six years, tours with The Jesus Lizard, Jawbox and Tar, and a friendship with Shellac that outlasted the records.

years.src: Star Tribune: Arcwelder wields its first new music in 24 years · Wikipedia: Arcwelder
years.p: The last of the run Bill Graber remembers making with [[Brian Paulson|65f13d3b-ddd6-4b33-8ab7-366ee7fb63c4]].
years.xp: On the road in these years Arcwelder toured with [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]], [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]] and [[Tar|5856ffe4-0171-495b-9986-03b96069200e]], and shared bills with [[Dirty Three|af8bb921-4d67-4f0d-ba17-6215315f92e4]], [[Pegboy|13e78eec-9ee4-47f2-a50e-2a9f519cb6e2]], Caspar Brötzmann and [[Cows|d4b064a0-5567-4930-a359-16fadfa7941b]].

years.src: Discogs: Arcwelder · Dig Me Out: Arcwelder history
years.h: Entropy comes out on Touch and Go as TG158
years.p: The fifth album, and the third on Touch and Go.

years.h: Shellac put all three names on the cover of The Futurist
years.p: [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]]'s 1997 album carries the names of Bill Graber, Rob Graber and Scott Macdonald.

q: The only practitioners of this style of rock that matter.
years.p: The sixth album, TG204. CMJ's Mike Wolf wrote that the band had done one thing only, propulsive, rhythmic, catchy rock, and was now nearly perfect at it.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Ryan Schreiber reviewed it in September 1999 and counted Arcwelder among the best Minnesota bands of the decade.

eras.title: Shellac keeps sending invitations
eras.text: No new records, but the band never fully stopped. Shellac brought them to All Tomorrow's Parties twice, Touch and Go put them on its 25th birthday bill, and First Avenue gave them a star on its outside wall.

years.h: Shellac's All Tomorrow's Parties wants Arcwelder
years.p: [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]] curate the UK festival and book Arcwelder. They do it again in 2012.

years.cap: Touch and Go's 25th anniversary, Chicago, September 2006
yt: Arcwelder at the Touch and Go 25th Anniversary
years.h: All three back on stage for Touch and Go's 25th
years.p: The original line-up plays the label's three-day anniversary party in Chicago.

years.cap: Rob Graber, Bill Graber and Scott Macdonald, c. 2017
years.h: Singing Grant Hart's parts at a benefit for Hart
years.p: [[Lori Barbero|e57b7efb-7dc6-4e6c-89f4-ee6314b213ed]] of Babes in Toyland invites the band to play three songs at a Hook and Ladder benefit for the Hüsker Dü drummer.
years.xp: "I'd practically shredded my voice trying to sing Grant's parts," Macdonald told The Current. Hart died that September.

eras.title: Twenty-four years later, Continue
eras.text: The band had been writing together again. They recorded at the Terrarium in Minneapolis and finished the mixes with J. Robbins of Jawbox, an old touring partner, and put it out themselves.

years.src: Star Tribune: Arcwelder wields its first new music in 24 years
years.h: 'Lafayette' and 'Take It Slow' end a 24-year silence
years.p: Two songs go up on the band's website and Bandcamp. Asked what took so long, Bill Graber said it was probably not a coincidence that his son Jon was turning 24.

years.src: Star Tribune: Arcwelder wields its first new music in 24 years · Discogs: Arcwelder
yt: Continue release show, Turf Club, January 2024
years.p: Tracked with Jason Orris at the Terrarium in Minneapolis and self-released. The Turf Club show to launch it is two sets, one new, one old.
years.xp: "J. has a great ear and really gets us in terms of what we want to sound like," Graber told the Star Tribune. He said it reminded him of the Jacket Made in Canada, Pull and Xerxes sessions with Paulson.
